Summary The luxury cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey was arrested in Singapore due to its owner's financial issues, with a law firm handling the detention.
 The US-based operator owes a supplier about US$500,000, and they suspended operations in Cambodia because of rising fuel costs due to the Iran war.
 After departing Cambodia with crew only, the ship was moved to Singapore by a lender, possibly for auction.

 Subscribe SINGAPORE, Nov 9 — Stranded luxury cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey has been “arrested” in Singapore following its owner’s financial struggles.
 Singapore law firm Helmsman LLC is listed as the arresting solicitor, according to court documents obtained by CBS News , reported the news agency today.
 A ship arrest is a legal process in which a vessel is detained by court order to secure a maritime claim.
 Its US-based operator Villa Vie Residences is said to owe one supplier approximately US$500,000 (RM2.03 million). It is unclear if the same supplier had hired the law firm to detain the liner.
 A check by AsiaOne shows the ship docked near Changi Bay.
 This comes after its operator announced on October 27 that they had suspended operations in Cambodia due to increasing fuel costs from the Iran war.
 On October 28, more than 200 passengers were given just seven hours to disembark from the cruise in Cambodia.
 The cruise ship departed Cambodia early on Wednesday (November 4), Reuters reported.
 The ship left with no passengers and around 50 crew, according to Taing Sochitkrishna, head of the Sihanoukville tourism department. He said then that around 100 passengers remained in Cambodia, while the others largely flew to other destinations in the region.
 Odyssey, which begun its voyage from Northern Ireland in October 2024, had promised a three-and-a-half-year continuous voyage where passengers could rent or purchase rooms on board while it travels to more than 150 countries, according to its website.
 The ship was later taken over by a lender and moved from Cambodia to Singapore ahead of a possible auction, reported CBS News on November 1. — AsiaOne
